platforms.why: NSIS needs the actual target .node/DLL/native subprocess bytes.
Installer configuration and launcher paths are inputs, rather than merely documentation.
Patched Electron/Sharp/native versions must be selected coherently; existing-version load probes can run now.
Artifact native-load results cannot be inferred from a development checkout.
Executable names, shortcuts and removal behavior must be tested on the produced installer.
Signing consumes the exact compiled installer and executable bytes.
Authenticode key/certificate/timestamp access is a concrete environment input.
Real updater transition requires two compatible signed versions and update metadata.
Publication consumes accepted notices/SBOM/provenance bound to actual shipped signed bytes.
Audio/document execution requires actual STT engines/models/FFmpeg and uv/Python/tool dependencies, not a picker or status fixture.
Verification consumes installed runtime wrappers and assets.
Only release-required native behavior justifies Windows transport implementation; Win-006.2 is conditional, not a prerequisite for supported TypeScript fallback.
Truthful fallback acceptance needs a written decision and capability negotiation tests.
Registration must match the actual application identity/executable.
Public callback/UX claims must refer to exact release artifacts.
Provider redirect registration, sandbox identity and callback ownership must be usable.
The final named app must contain the staged architecture-correct .node/executable bytes; naming/script repair and preliminary app builds can begin before this output exists.
Target Electron/Sharp/libSQL/ABI selections feed final stage manifest; preliminary current-version probes can start now.
Executable and .node load tests consume actual arm64/x64 bundles.
Signing/notarization consumes real built apps/DMG/ZIP inputs.
Final nested executable/module inventory defines signing scope.
Valid Developer ID and Apple notarization access are concrete prerequisites.
Minimum OS must be derived for the actual selected Electron release, especially after security upgrade.
macOS updater consumes signed compatible app/ZIP versions and manifests.
Two actual release versions are needed for download/install/relaunch.
Exact signed artifact supply-chain acceptance precedes public publishing.
Effective entitlements and installed launch environment differ from terminal dev mode.
Actual nondeveloper STT/FFmpeg/uv/Python/Git tools and assets must exist.
Runtime backend/transport choice determines which signed sidecar binaries must ship.
Dock, sleep, quit, signing and subprocess behavior must be observed in installed release app.
Observed Bun1.3.14 PASS/Bun1.4.2 FAIL requires an enforced qualified version before accepting final bundle.
Patched image native dependency versions are actual build inputs.
Private single-instance versus multi-user product scope determines principal/tenant policy; no requirement to build SaaS for a declared private deployment.
If multi-user collaboration is advertised, identity/membership enforcement must be joined to the actual workspace service.
Deployment consumes a launchable image/bundle, not just renderer static assets.
Trusted forwarding and cookie/WS security must use actual auth assumptions.
Domain/TLS, runtime access and persistence are concrete resources; local reverse proxy tests can start now.
Server must bind uploaded/downloaded resource IDs to authorized principal/workspace.
Persisted resource IDs, size/checksum/MIME and tool-readable bytes must agree across files RPC and artifact storage.
Acknowledged permitted workspace rather than URL text determines effective scope.
Unsupported desktop operations must be classified consistently with each UI/runtime capability.
HTTPS callback registration, grants, refresh and revoke require real supported provider account.
Click target must preserve actual workspace/session navigation semantics.
Browser codecs/bytes must feed actual server STT/media jobs.
A real browser engine/profile/remote interaction endpoint is required; a visible panel is insufficient.
Every enabled/unsupported route must have truthful behavior before final all-surface certification.
Final browser evidence consumes the deployed transport and real public security context.
Each enabled feature journey waits only for its own integrated backend/resource/UI outputs; no blanket wait before error recovery implementation.
Viewer ES library/runtime errors need a passing actual viewer build/type graph.
The existing Pages Functions/R2 API needs actual binding/origin/owner-key configuration.
Export/shared data must remove secret and private references before public viewer read.
Final evidence must compile the exact post-merge source, while current-head repair/probes can start immediately.
Controls must be exercised in a runnable app/server; harness and test data can be built now.
Only relevant feature implementations/credentials/resources are required; fixtures cannot close real provider behavior.
Native accessibility trees and browser focus behavior must come from the real target runtime.
Production artifact and real service resource topology determine startup/memory/load results.
Expected data sizes/users/concurrency and budget thresholds are acceptance inputs, not scheduling assumptions.
Static preferences/updated manifests cannot prove effective sandbox/native lib behavior; controlled installed allowed/denied probes consume built runtime.
Security scenarios need the declared authenticated ownership policy.
Canonical documents/SQLite/attachments/encrypted keys define exactly what must be saved and restored.
Observed process/disk/ownership behavior requires runnable target services.
Need exact signed installer, not dev checkout.
Need exact signed/notarized artifact with effective entitlements.
Updater downloads/installs compatible actual version pair and manifests.
Seed/readback scope follows the explicit supported retention policy.
Actual deployed supervisor/volumes/proxy must be exercised.
Required workers/provider/browser/data dependencies determine healthy versus degraded/failed states.
SBOM/provenance binds the bytes that ship, including native libraries/runtime/model/tool assets; source-only dependency report is insufficient.
Instructions must invoke actual supported setup/feature behavior.
A real install/deploy/restore target is required to verify written instructions.
All adopted PR/dirty changes and superseded/squash branches must resolve to immutable exact source; inventory starts before merging.
A task closes from its own acceptance outputs, not its parent status or branch name.
Freeze one feature-preserving merged candidate; source planning does not wait for freeze.
Target install reads exact frozen release bytes.
Read deployed revision and execute genuine public/private-instance workflows.
Exact shipped components/risks/licenses and provenance must be accepted.
Final usability/regression evidence must use the exact accepted artifact/deployment.
Every advertised user journey needs genuine evidence rather than fixture substitution.
Actual deployed/installed negative boundary results must accompany signoff.
Need measured accepted target budgets.
New-user/operator setup and recovery must be reproducible.

services.title: Configuration and origin
services.boundary: Aliases/root precedence and public URL/cookie fields; domain owners own service-specific config values, contract owner merges resolver/bootstrap edits.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Serialized protocol and capability routing
services.boundary: Versioned payload/error/event/workspace shapes; one owner merges transport dispatcher edits, domain owners own handlers and executable conformance tests.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Principal, tenant and grant authority
services.boundary: Principal/issuer and grants/fences; hosted identity is coordinated with WEB-002.1/002.2. Native root/fence changes proposed by SVC-038.1 are reviewed here, not edited concurrently.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Protected credentials and secret projections
services.boundary: Master-key provider and secretRef/scope/revoke generations; domains own OAuth/mail/import adapters, not shared credential backend.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: OMP runtime/protocol and authoritative transcript
services.boundary: One protocol owner reconciles committed17.2.10 with dirty18.4.12 decoder/negotiate changes. SVC-005.2 owns branch/skill tests and proposes branch functions as isolated patch.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: OS subprocess ownership and cleanup
services.boundary: Process tree/argv/cwd/env/exit and Windows JobObject adapter; domain processes remain independently owned. Secret projection changes belong to SECRET; lifecycle implementation to domain/PROCESS.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Runtime versions and artifact closure
services.boundary: One manifest/version owner interfaces with WIN/MAC/WEB packaging. Helper/executable builders stay with platform owners. Domain owners supply required artifacts and startup probes.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Sources/MCP pool and least-authority tools
services.boundary: Per-owner source/pool identity, tool schemas, dynamic credentials and disposal; standalone session adapter is SVC-008.1 and provider-specific files stay with domain owners.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Cloud/local run state and result receipts
services.boundary: Run state/exit/artifact/progress schema and provisioning gate. SVC-012.2 owns measurements, SVC-013.1 gate branch, SVC-014.2 durable registry; common provider pump edits merged by this owner.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Messaging binding and delivery schema
services.boundary: Shared binding, message ID/approval/dedupe/receipt schema; five adapter/worker owners own their subdirectories. SVC-016.2 handles gateway lifecycle/queue patch, core dispatcher changes go through this owner.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: External effect identity and unknown outcomes
services.boundary: Persist-before-effect, unknown-outcome and durable terminal history contract. Occurrence schema/cron are SVC-023.1; retry/webhook are SVC-022.1; owners exchange effect IDs instead of serializing whole domains.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Portable SQLite API and schema ownership
services.boundary: Adapter API and runtime pins exclusively here. Each consumer owns its own schema/transaction/migration files; SVC-040.2 coordinates compatibility without rewriting consumer-owned code. FTS port/capability belongs to SVC-025.1.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: One canonical writer and durable journal ACK
services.boundary: Expected revision/op signature and trusted receipt producer. Domain owners own project/task/page handlers and clients; outbox recovery SVC-027.2 proposes consumer changes under receipt contract. No second canonical writer.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Cost reservation, usage and settlement
services.boundary: Provider usage/operation identity/settlement schema. SVC-039.2 owns crash/concurrency tests and recovery transition patch; cloud cost consumer SVC-012.2 supplies usage without duplicating this ledger.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Catalog trust and atomic installation
services.boundary: Catalog/key policy and immutable refs; SVC-030.2 owns installer and local-edit protection. Tool installs delegate through existing toolchain contract.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.

services.title: Persisted consent and egress policy
services.boundary: Actor/purpose consent, wake/ASR gating and retention. Voice adapter/playback is SVC-041.2; gamification analytics consumer SVC-036.2 follows same consent projection.
services.concurrencyRule: One designated owner edits/promotes changes to these shared contract files. Consumers own their domain files, test fixtures and isolated proposed patches; shared-file overlap is a patch coordination constraint, not a whole-project task dependency.
